speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment, could you please tell me how many weeks along you are in your pregnancy and when the bleeding and abdominal pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to ask if the abdominal pain is constant and localized, rather than coming in waves like normal labor contractions. Also, does the abdomen feel rigid or tender to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of a prior cesarean section and the sudden onset of severe, constant abdominal pain with bleeding, I am deeply concerned about uterine rupture. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Exam; REQUEST TEST: Fetal_Heart_Rate_Monitoring

text: RESULTS: Abdominal Examination: Mild distension, decreased bowel sounds, tympanic sound predominating, diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding. Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring: Shows recurrent variable decelerations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of recurrent variable decelerations and your history of a prior cesarean section are highly concerning for uterine rupture or placental abruption. I need to confirm the placental location and fetal status immediately, so REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_Abdomen and REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound Abdomen and Pelvis: Suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum. Complete Blood Count: Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL (decreased), Platelets 200,000 /μL.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of uterine wall disruption and hemoperitoneum, combined with your history and symptoms, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture
